Dear Colleague,

I recently saw Joshua Wood, a 79-year-old male, consultation on May 22, 2026, as requested. I hope this summary will be of assistance in your evaluation of his life insurance application. 

Mr. Wood has a history of prostate adenocarcinoma, which was diagnosed approximately 15.3 years ago, with a Gleason score of 7. He underwent a radical prostatectomy and has been in controlled status since. His most recent PSA levels are undetectable, indicating no evidence of disease recurrence. There are no current medications prescribed for his prostate condition.

Additionally, Mr. Wood has been managing eczema since September Z024. This condition is currently well-controlled with the use of triamcinolone topical 0.1%. During the examination, I noted no acute exacerbations of the eczema, and his skin appeared healthy with no signs of active inflammation.

Furthermore, Mr. Wood has a history of acne, which began in August 2021. He is currently controlling his acne with a regimen that includes minocycline 100 mg and doxycycline 100 mg. His skin examination revealed no active acne lesions, and he reported satisfaction with his current treatment plan.

Mr. Wood also has erectile dysfunction, which started in April 2024. This condition is currently managed with tadalafil 5 mg as needed. He reports that this medication is effective in achieving and maintaining an erection sufficient for sexual activity.

In addition, Mr. Wood has rosacea, which began on September 14, 2024. He is currently using metronidazole topical 1% and ivermectin topical 1% to manage his symptoms. His facial skin showed no signs of active rosacea during the examination.

During his last visit on May 22, 2026, Mr. Wood's blood pressure was recorded at 142/91 mmHg, and his weight was 143 pounds. His vital signs were otherwise within normal limits. I also noted that Mr. Wood has a history of tobacco use, having smoked approximately 1.5 packs per day since October 2001. He successfully quit smoking in June 2024. His alcohol consumption is minimal, averaging about one drink per week.

Family history is significant for myocardial infarction in his mother, who developed the condition at age 46 and passed away at age 57. His father, currently alive at 90 years old, has a history of Alzheimer's disease, which began at age 73.

In summary, Mr. Wood's current medical conditions are well-controlled with appropriate treatments. His social history includes a past tobacco use and minimal alcohol consumption.
